Project-specific Java correctness contract:
- Board is the sole owner of one authoritative 4x4 int grid; getGridCopy() returns a deep read-only snapshot, so Game and spawners must never try to mutate the board through getGridCopy()
- declare one exact mutation API void setCell(int row, int col, int value) with bounds checks and 0-or-power-of-two validation, and use it consistently for deterministic setup and applying every Spawn; do not invent setGridValue, placeTile, setTile, or aliases
- declare boolean hasTileAtLeast(int value) on Board and use that exact name for win detection; do not invent hasValueAtLeast or aliases
- declare a simple immutable MoveResult with exact accessors boolean changed() and int scoreGained(); Board.move(Direction) returns it, and Game must use these methods rather than fields
- Board.move must implement each row/column by reading exactly four values in movement order, compacting nonzero values, merging one equal adjacent pair at most once, compacting/filling with zero, writing all four results back to the authoritative grid, and summing each newly merged tile into scoreGained; forbid generic multi-delta helpers with unused or ambiguous row/column parameters
- Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, adds scoreGained, and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true; apply the Spawn via Board.setCell, never via a copied array
- Game must update status after every move attempt, including an unchanged move: WON iff Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048), otherwise LOST iff !Board.hasAnyMoves(), otherwise IN_PROGRESS
- initialization/reset must clear the authoritative Board and apply exactly two spawns through Board.setCell; a deterministic SequenceSpawner must consume its documented sequence in order
- keep MainTest to 2--4 concise deterministic tests using only the canonical methods; do not assert mutations made to arrays returned by getGridCopy()
- repeat the exact getGridCopy immutability, setCell, hasTileAtLeast, MoveResult, line-merge, spawn-on-change, and status-transition rules in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task; vague descriptions are insufficient

Domain Reasoning: Entity: Board owns authoritative 4x4 int grid; only mutation path is setCell(row,col,value) with strict validation.
Entity: Game orchestrates Board, score, status, and spawning boundary; applies spawns through Board.setCell only when a move changed the grid.
Entity: MoveResult (immutable) carries exactly two accessors: changed() and scoreGained(); used by Game to update score and decide spawn.
Entity: Direction enum for LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN; Board.move(Direction) processes lines deterministically with single-merge-per-line rule.
Boundary: Spawner interface returns deterministic spawn instructions; SequenceSpawner consumes a documented sequence in order.
Rules: Win when Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048); Lose when no moves remain; Otherwise IN_PROGRESS. Status updated after every move attempt.
Constraints: getGridCopy() returns deep immutable snapshot; callers must not mutate Board through it.
Initialization/reset: clear board and apply exactly two spawns via Board.setCell using SequenceSpawner.
Domain Expectations: Board.move(Direction) compacts nonzeros per line, merges one adjacent equal pair at most once, compacts again, writes back exactly 4 values.
MoveResult.changed() is true if any cell changed after the move; scoreGained() sums only newly formed merged tile values.
Game.move(Direction) calls Board.move once, increments score by scoreGained(), and spawns exactly one tile only when changed() is true.
Board.getGridCopy() returns a deep copy; external mutations to this array never affect Board state.
Board.setCell(row,col,value) enforces bounds and 0-or-power-of-two validation; used for all deterministic setup and spawns.
Win detection uses Board.hasTileAtLeast(2048) exactly; loss when no moves are possible via Board.hasAnyMoves().
SequenceSpawner provides deterministic (row,col,value) triples; consumed strictly in order for initialization and subsequent spawns.
Reset clears Board and score, sets status to IN_PROGRESS, and applies exactly two initial spawns via Board.setCell.
Product Goals: Deliver correct, deterministic 2048 core mechanics with clean API
Keep architecture small, readable, and testable
Ensure automated build and concise tests pass reliably
User Stories: As a player, I can make moves in four directions and see the board update according to 2048 rules.
As a player, I can see my score increase when tiles merge and understand the deterministic spawn behavior.
As a player, I receive clear game status updates: IN_PROGRESS, WON at 2048, or LOST when no moves remain.
As a developer, I can reset the game to a known deterministic state for testing and demos.
Competitive Analysis: Original 2048 (Gabriele Cirulli): browser-based, random spawning; reference mechanics.
Open-source Java console 2048 clones: varying structure and testability; often mix UI and logic.
Threes!: conceptual predecessor with different merge mechanics; stricter spawning rules.
Mobile 2048 variants: add animations and UIs but rarely expose deterministic logic APIs.

Requirement Analysis: We must implement a Java 11 Maven project with an entry Main.java in the default package and exactly one test file MainTest.java using JUnit Jupiter. The pom.xml must declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5. The core domain includes Board, Game, Direction, MoveResult, and a deterministic SequenceSpawner boundary. Board exclusively owns the 4x4 grid, exposes getGridCopy() as an immutable deep copy, validates and applies all mutations via setCell(row,col,value), implements deterministic line-based movement with single-merge-per-line, and reports MoveResult with changed() and scoreGained(). Game coordinates moves, applies spawn exactly once on changes via Board.setCell, accumulates score, and updates status after every move. Initialization/reset applies exactly two spawns via SequenceSpawner. Tests must be concise, deterministic, and headless, covering wiring (Main) and a representative core rule (e.g., merge and spawn-on-change). Architecture should separate domain logic from runtime demo and from the deterministic spawner boundary, ensuring no GUI and no random dependencies.
